Based on the clinical presentation of acute abdomen, imaging findings, and his prior history of appendectomy, an alternative etiology was initially suspected, prompting an open surgical approach. Regarding the surgical procedure performed: An infraumbilical incision was made, with dissection through the layers until entering the right abdominal cavity, where an edematous and erythematous appendiceal stump was found, confirming the diagnosis of stump appendicitis (Figure 2A). The stump was ligated at its base, the inflammatory phlegmon was dissected, and stump appendectomy was performed (Figure 2B) using the Halstead technique. claims.text: A 48-year-old man described as from Chihuahua, Mexico, with appendectomy several years earlier, presented with four days of continuous right-lower-quadrant pain, two diarrhea episodes and two fevers above 38 °C. GP butyl hyoscine/metoclopramide did not help. Examination showed an appendectomy scar, absent bowel sounds, distension, rebound/McBurney/psoas/obturator signs, involuntary rigidity and superficial-touch pain. WBC was printed as 14.55 cells/mm³ with reference 4.5–10.5; neutrophils 8.93 cells/mm³ were described without neutrophilia, with no inferred multiplier. Oral-contrast CT showed pericecal fat inflammation and phlegmon; constipation, gastroenteritis and right-sided diverticulitis were considered then refuted. Open emergency exploration through an infraumbilical incision confirmed an edematous erythematous appendiceal stump. Base ligation, phlegmon dissection and Halstead completion appendectomy were followed by irrigation/layered closure. Diagnostic laparoscopy was unavailable because of missing equipment. A caption AI-estimated stump length 0.67 cm requires review. Good postoperative progress the following day prompted indicated home discharge with unspecified analgesic/antibiotic treatment; actual discharge completion is not explicit. Histopathology obtained weeks later showed acute fibrinopurulent appendicitis, purulent peritonitis and a 4×4 cm phlegmon. At a consultation reported one month later he continued to improve and was discharged from surgical care.

The stump was ligated at its base, the inflammatory phlegmon was dissected, and stump appendectomy was performed (Figure 2B) using the Halstead technique. The abdominal cavity was then irrigated, followed by layered closure, and the procedure was concluded. Diagnostic laparoscopy was not performed, as the necessary equipment was unavailable at our hospital.
